content: To maintain overall health and reduce the risk of certain diseases, it is important to adopt lifestyle changes such as engaging in regular physical activity, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and consuming a well-balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store your medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medications according to local disposal guidelines. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the medication. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. This medication is a form of estrogen, a hormone used by women to alleviate symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to decreased estrogen production in the body. Certain estrogen products may also be prescribed to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis) in postmenopausal women. However, other medications, such as raloxifene or bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate), may also be effective and potentially safer for preventing bone loss. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. If you are prescribed extended-release tablets, do not crush, chew, or dissolve them, as this can release the drug all at once, increasing the risk of side effects. Take the medication regularly at the same time each day to maximize its benefits. Follow your prescribed dosing schedule carefully. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal complications such as blood clots (e.g., heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs). Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. If you experience serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing due to an overdose, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S. or 1-844-764-7669 in Canada). Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. These include reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking. Engage in mental exercises, such as reading or solving puzzles, to help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, incorporate weight-bearing exercises, avoid smoking, limit alcohol intake, and consume a diet with sufficient calcium and vitamin D.
